text: What type of epithelium lines the alveoli of the lungs?
explanation: Simple squamous epithelium allows for efficient gas exchange.

text: What is the function of the Golgi apparatus?
explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins.

text: Which organelle contains digestive enzymes?
explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes for digestion.

text: What type of connective tissue stores fat?
explanation: Adipose tissue stores fat and provides insulation.

text: Which of the following is a characteristic of cardiac muscle?
explanation: Cardiac muscle has intercalated discs that allow for coordinated contraction.

text: What type of epithelium is found in the bladder?
explanation: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) stretches to accommodate urine volume.

text: Which cell type produces antibodies?
explanation: Plasma cells are differentiated B lymphocytes that secrete antibodies.

text: What is the primary function of rough endoplasmic reticulum?
explanation: Rough ER is studded with ribosomes for protein synthesis.

text: Which stain is used to visualize elastic fibers?
explanation: Verhoeff-Van Gieson stain specifically highlights elastic fibers in black.

text: What type of cartilage is found in the intervertebral discs?
explanation: Fibrocartilage provides strength and resists compression in intervertebral discs.

text: Which cells line the blood-brain barrier?
explanation: Tight junctions between endothelial cells form the blood-brain barrier.

text: What is the most abundant protein in the extracellular matrix?
explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the ECM, providing structural support.

text: Which type of collagen forms reticular fibers?
explanation: Type III collagen forms reticular fibers that support soft organs.

text: Where are Paneth cells located?
explanation: Paneth cells reside in intestinal crypts and secrete antimicrobial peptides.

text: What type of epithelium lines the trachea?
explanation: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells lines the trachea.

text: Which organelle is responsible for ATP production?
explanation: Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.

text: What is the function of microvilli?
explanation: Microvilli increase surface area for absorption, especially in the small intestine.

text: Which cells produce myelin in the central nervous system?
explanation: Oligodendrocytes myelinate axons in the CNS; Schwann cells do so in the PNS.

text: What is the main component of the basal lamina?
explanation: Type IV collagen forms the meshwork of the basal lamina.

text: Which bone cells are responsible for bone resorption?
explanation: Osteoclasts are multinucleated cells that resorb bone.

text: What type of gland secretes its product directly into the bloodstream?
explanation: Endocrine glands are ductless and secrete hormones into the blood.

text: Which staining method is used to demonstrate carbohydrates?
explanation: PAS stain highlights glycogen and mucopolysaccharides.

text: What is the function of tight junctions?
explanation: Tight junctions seal adjacent epithelial cells to prevent leakage.

text: Which cells are responsible for producing cerebrospinal fluid?
explanation: Ependymal cells line the ventricles and produce CSF.

text: What type of epithelium is found in the kidney glomerulus?
explanation: The glomerular filtration barrier is made of simple squamous epithelium (podocytes).

text: Which cells in the liver are responsible for phagocytosis?
explanation: Kupffer cells are liver macrophages that remove debris and pathogens.

text: What is the characteristic feature of skeletal muscle under microscopy?
explanation: Skeletal muscle has striations and peripherally located multiple nuclei.

text: Which cell type is the most abundant in the epidermis?
explanation: Keratinocytes make up 90% of epidermal cells and produce keratin.

text: What is the function of the nucleolus?
explanation: The nucleolus is where rRNA is transcribed and ribosome subunits assemble.

text: Which connective tissue cell produces histamine?
explanation: Mast cells release histamine during inflammatory and allergic responses.

text: What type of cartilage forms the fetal skeleton?
explanation: Hyaline cartilage forms the temporary fetal skeleton before ossification.

text: Which structure connects the cytoplasm of adjacent cardiac muscle cells?
explanation: Gap junctions allow electrical coupling and synchronized contraction.

text: What is the primary function of smooth endoplasmic reticulum in liver cells?
explanation: SER in hepatocytes detoxifies drugs and synthesizes lipids.

text: Which cells line the central canal of the spinal cord?
explanation: Ependymal cells are ciliated epithelial cells lining the central canal.

text: What type of gland secretes sebum?
explanation: Sebaceous glands are holocrine glands that release entire cells as sebum.

text: Which layer of the skin contains blood vessels and nerves?
explanation: The dermis is vascularized and innervated; the epidermis is avascular.

text: What is the function of cilia?
options: Movement of substances across cell surface
explanation: Cilia beat rhythmically to move mucus or other substances.

text: Which cell type is responsible for bone formation?
explanation: Osteoblasts synthesize and deposit bone matrix.

text: What is the most common cell in connective tissue proper?
explanation: Fibroblasts are the most abundant connective tissue cells, producing ECM.

text: Which organelle is involved in autophagy?
explanation: Lysosomes degrade damaged organelles through autophagy.

text: What type of epithelium lines the esophagus?
explanation: The esophagus is lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium.

text: Which cells produce surfactant in the lungs?
explanation: Type II pneumocytes secrete pulmonary surfactant to reduce surface tension.

text: What is the function of a desmosome?
explanation: Desmosomes are anchoring junctions that provide mechanical strength.

text: Which stain is used to visualize reticular fibers?
explanation: Reticular fibers are argyrophilic and stain black with silver.

text: What is the primary cell type in the thyroid follicle?
explanation: Follicular cells produce thyroid hormones T3 and T4.

text: Which layer of the epidermis contains stem cells?
explanation: The stratum basale contains keratinocyte stem cells.

text: What is the function of Weibel-Palade bodies?
explanation: Weibel-Palade bodies in endothelial cells store vWF and P-selectin.

text: Which cells are responsible for maintaining the blood-testis barrier?
explanation: Sertoli cells form tight junctions creating the blood-testis barrier.

text: What type of muscle is found in the walls of blood vessels?
explanation: Smooth muscle in vessel walls controls vasoconstriction and vasodilation.

text: What is the primary component of elastic cartilage?
explanation: Elastic cartilage contains abundant elastic fibers for flexibility.

text: Which cells are the primary phagocytes in the brain?
explanation: Microglia are the resident macrophages of the CNS.

text: What is the function of the brush border?
explanation: The brush border (microvilli) increases surface area for absorption.

text: Which organelle is prominent in cells active in protein secretion?
explanation: Rough ER is abundant in protein-secreting cells like plasma cells.

text: Where is hyaline cartilage found in adults?
explanation: Hyaline cartilage covers articular surfaces of bones in joints.

text: Which cells produce the myelin sheath in the peripheral nervous system?
explanation: Schwann cells myelinate axons in the PNS.

text: What type of epithelium lines the stomach?
explanation: The stomach is lined by simple columnar epithelium with mucus-secreting cells.

text: Which cells in the pancreas produce insulin?
explanation: Beta cells of the pancreatic islets produce insulin.

text: What is the function of gap junctions?
explanation: Gap junctions allow direct passage of ions and small molecules between cells.

text: Which stain is used to demonstrate lipids?
explanation: Oil Red O stains neutral lipids and fat droplets.

text: What is the main cell type in the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex?
explanation: The zona glomerulosa secretes mineralocorticoids, primarily aldosterone.

text: Which structures are found in the portal triad?
options: Hepatic artery, portal vein, bile duct
Kupffer cells, stellate cells, bile canaliculi
explanation: The portal triad contains a branch of hepatic artery, portal vein, and bile duct.

text: What type of epithelium is found in the gallbladder?
explanation: The gallbladder is lined by simple columnar epithelium specialized for absorption.

text: Which cells in the kidney form the juxtaglomerular apparatus?
options: Proximal tubule cells and loop of Henle
explanation: The macula densa and juxtaglomerular cells form the JGA, regulating blood pressure.

text: What is the function of osteocytes?
explanation: Osteocytes are mature bone cells that maintain the bone matrix.

text: Which layer of the epidermis contains keratohyalin granules?
explanation: The stratum granulosum contains keratohyalin granules that help form keratin.

text: What type of gland is the sweat gland?
explanation: Eccrine sweat glands are merocrine glands secreting via exocytosis.

text: Which cells are responsible for bone remodeling?
explanation: Osteoblasts form bone while osteoclasts resorb it, maintaining remodeling.

text: What is the characteristic of stratified squamous keratinized epithelium?
options: Has a layer of dead cells
explanation: Keratinized epithelium has a superficial layer of dead, keratin-filled cells (skin).

text: Which organelle contains catalase?
explanation: Peroxisomes contain catalase to break down hydrogen peroxide.

text: What type of cells line the ventricles of the brain?
explanation: Ependymal cells are ciliated cuboidal cells lining the brain ventricles.

text: Which cells in the stomach produce hydrochloric acid?
explanation: Parietal cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor.

text: What is the function of the centrosome?
explanation: The centrosome organizes microtubules and forms the mitotic spindle.

text: Which type of collagen is found in the basement membrane?
explanation: Type IV collagen forms the network of the basement membrane.

text: What is the primary function of the zona fasciculata?
explanation: The zona fasciculata secretes glucocorticoids, mainly cortisol.

text: Which cells are the first to respond to tissue injury?
explanation: Neutrophils are the first leukocytes to arrive at sites of acute inflammation.

text: What is the function of the sarcomere?
explanation: The sarcomere is the basic contractile unit of striated muscle.

text: Which cells line the proximal convoluted tubule?
explanation: PCT cells are simple cuboidal with prominent microvilli (brush border).

text: What is the function of Nissl bodies?
explanation: Nissl bodies are rough ER in neurons, involved in protein synthesis.

text: Which structure is found in the hilum of the lymph node?
explanation: Efferent lymphatic vessels exit the lymph node at the hilum.

text: What type of epithelium is found in the uterine tube (fallopian tube)?
explanation: The fallopian tube has ciliated simple columnar epithelium to move the ovum.

text: Which cells in the testis produce testosterone?
explanation: Leydig cells (interstitial cells) produce testosterone.

text: What is the function of the stria vascularis?
explanation: The stria vascularis in the cochlea produces endolymph rich in potassium.

text: Which cells surround the cell body of a neuron in ganglia?
explanation: Satellite cells provide support and insulation to neuronal cell bodies in ganglia.

text: What type of epithelium is found in the cornea?
explanation: The cornea has stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium for protection.

text: Which cells in the pituitary gland produce growth hormone?
explanation: Somatotrophs (acidophils) in the anterior pituitary produce GH.

text: What is the function of the T-tubule system in muscle?
explanation: T-tubules conduct action potentials deep into the muscle fiber for coordinated contraction.

text: Which cells are found in the red pulp of the spleen?
explanation: The red pulp contains macrophages and red blood cells for filtration and storage.

text: What type of cartilage is found in the epiglottis?
explanation: The epiglottis contains elastic cartilage for flexibility.

text: Which stain is used for reticular fibers?
explanation: Silver stain (reticulin stain) highlights reticular fibers black.

text: What is the function of podocytes?
explanation: Podocytes form the visceral layer of Bowman's capsule and participate in filtration.

text: Which cells produce calcitonin?
explanation: Parafollicular cells (C cells) of the thyroid secrete calcitonin.

text: What is the characteristic feature of elastic cartilage?
explanation: Elastic cartilage has numerous elastic fibers in its matrix.

text: Which cells in the small intestine produce lysozyme?
explanation: Paneth cells secrete lysozyme and other antimicrobial proteins.

text: What is the function of the enamel organ?
explanation: The enamel organ produces enamel during tooth development.

text: Which cells are responsible for the blood-brain barrier?
explanation: The BBB consists of endothelial tight junctions, astrocyte end-feet, and pericytes.

text: What type of epithelium lines the endocervical canal?
explanation: The endocervix is lined by mucus-secreting simple columnar epithelium.

text: Which cells produce CSF in the choroid plexus?
explanation: Specialized choroid epithelial cells (modified ependymal cells) produce CSF.

text: What is the function of the myoepithelial cells in salivary glands?
explanation: Myoepithelial cells contract to propel saliva from acini into ducts.

text: Which layer of the heart contains cardiac muscle?
explanation: The myocardium is the muscular layer of the heart composed of cardiac muscle.

text: What is the function of the macula densa?
explanation: Macula densa cells detect tubular fluid NaCl concentration to regulate GFR.
